significance.justification: Verified true, the claim would establish a form-(iii) predictive coupling and temporal ordering: successful jailbreaks exhibit an "elevated-then-decaying (collapse)" refusal trajectory before harmful continuation, while refusals rise and benign responses remain low; it also adds the form-(ii) causal result that intervention "only at the collapse point" can halt the jailbreak. This fixes expectations about when refusal fails and links a measurable internal trajectory to later behavior, extending the static causal refusal-direction picture used in Arditi et al., "Refusal in Language Models Is Mediated by a Single Direction," into a dynamical account; it establishes both a behavioral phenomenon and a causal mechanism rather than merely decodability. A negative result would rule out delayed commitment collapse as a general explanation or early-warning signature across the asserted attack classes, although it would not rule out attack-specific dynamics or static refusal mechanisms, and the true and false states are clearly distinguishable. Topic-substitution check: replacing the trajectory, collapse signature, and timing relation with generic mechanistic LLM safety would not merit this score; the specific temporal law is materially stronger than the topic's obvious probe-and-steer hypothesis.

reach.justification: The transferable handles are explicitly the per-token "refusal commitment trajectory," an "early-warning monitor," a detected "collapse point," and a "minimal one-shot repair" that re-injects the refusal direction. The monitor is ex ante relative to harmful continuation because it uses the "first k generated tokens" to predict eventual jailbreak success and can trigger repair before commitment, although it provides less lead time for attacks that become harmful immediately. The hypothesis asserts the same trajectory relation across multiple open-weight model families and diverse jailbreak classes, so after per-model direction extraction it predicts a rise-versus-collapse pattern rather than merely supplying a procedure; downstream users include safety auditors and deployers able to access internal activations, but not closed-model users or outside-AI practitioners. Topic-substitution check: generic interpretability-based safety supplies none of these timed diagnostic and intervention handles, so the reach comes from this claim rather than from the topic itself.
